program_name: Challenging the Frontiers of Poverty Reduction (CFPR)
intervention_description: Grant-based approach combining asset transfer, subsistence allowance, livelihood support services, health support, and social awareness for extreme poor women

graduation_components_rationale.consumption_support: Subsistence allowance mentioned as part of support package
graduation_components_rationale.healthcare: Regular health services and health worker support provided
graduation_components_rationale.assets: Productive asset transfer is a core component of the programme
graduation_components_rationale.skills_training: Livelihood support services and training mentioned
graduation_components_rationale.savings: Programme encourages savings behavior among participants
graduation_components_rationale.coaching: Programme organizers make regular household visits and provide guidance
graduation_components_rationale.social_empowerment: Social Development programme designed to increase awareness and empower participants

outcomes.outcome_description: Value of houses in Bangladeshi Taka (BDT)
outcomes.literal_text: On average, the value of the houses went up by BDT 1197 (US $ 17.16) due to programme participation and this increase was found to be statistically significant at the 5% level

outcomes.outcome_description: Cash savings amount in Bangladeshi Taka (BDT) per participant woman
outcomes.literal_text: Effect on savings was BDT 1564 (US $22.42) per participant woman on average

outcomes.outcome_description: Percentage increase in sanitary latrine holdings
outcomes.literal_text: Sanitary latrine holdings increased by 36% among the participant households as a net effect of the programme

outcomes.outcome_description: Awareness index measuring social, political, and legal awareness (0-1 scale)
outcomes.literal_text: Difference-in-difference of awareness index bears positive sign and is statistically significant 1% level

outcomes.outcome_description: Total food expenditure in Bangladeshi Taka (BDT)
outcomes.literal_text: Total food expenditure was found to be, on average, BDT 16.70 more for the treatment households, compared to the control households and this is significant at the 5% level

outcomes.outcome_description: Credit market participation and outstanding loan amounts
outcomes.literal_text: Analyzing the amount of outstanding loans, it was found that the difference-in-difference is statistically insignificant indicating that programme participation had no impact on credit market participation
outcomes.text_position: Results section, Credit market participation paragraph
